sections.summary: Dijkstra argues that programs should make the relationship between static text and dynamic execution easy to understand. Structured sequencing, conditionals, procedures, and loops provide independent coordinates for reasoning about progress and variable values, whereas unrestricted jumps obscure them; mechanically eliminating jumps alone does not restore clarity.
